elements.text: Grinds ore and ingots into dust. One ore gives two dust, so you get twice as much metal as smelting the ore directly.
It also grinds vanilla items: bones into bone meal, amethyst into amethyst dust, quartz into silicon dust, wool into string, cobblestone into gravel.
Smelts the same things as a regular furnace, but on power and twice as fast. It needs no fuel, so it is easy to put into an automated line.
Presses things together: fiber and mesh into dense plates, snowballs, clay, sand and ice into blocks, leaves and seeds into biomass. Some parts can only be made in it.
It has two modes, switched with a button in its window. **Rolling** turns an ingot into plates; **extruding** turns a plate into wire, and some ingots into rods and fiber.
Pulls the useful part out of whatever you put in: rubber from resin, resin from resin leaves, leather from rotten flesh. It does not crush anything, it just extracts.
Washes ore with water. One ore gives three dust instead of the crusher's two, and sometimes a rare metal drops on top.
Pour water straight into the machine with buckets or feed it through a pipe.

Turns one item into another. Put the item in the input, the right **catalyst** in its slot, and feed it power. Once it has stored as much energy as the transformation costs, the result appears in the output.
The restructor has no work time, only energy: the more power you give it, the faster it goes. Catalysts come in tiers, and the higher the tier, the more valuable the transformations.

The **Restructor T2** runs three transformations at once on one catalyst and spends half as much of the source item on each: a block the T1 uses up in one transformation lasts it two. The energy cost stays the same.

Mixes an item with a fluid to make a new fluid. Lapis dust with water gives **coolant**, mineral dust with water gives **drill fluid**. Once you have the cryo chamber, coolant can be made from blue ice and water, no lapis needed.
Melts items into a fluid, but only if heat from the heat network reaches it. Amethyst becomes molten amethyst, and a lead ingot becomes molten lead.
A capsule holds 1000 mB of any fluid. The **capsule filler** pours fluid into it from its own tank, and a full capsule can go straight into a crafting recipe.
Splits one thing into several: you put in one input and get several different products at once. It is used where a regular machine would give only one.

Makes cryo rods. The first one is built from an empty rod and cryolite, the second from the first and cryo crystals, the third from the second and a capsule of superfluid condensate. It also twists superconducting wire into strands.
Rods wear out in the cryo chamber over time, so the fabricator never runs out of work.

Grows and multiplies items using water. What it grows depends on the upgrade: the **biostimulator** for plants, the **crystal resonator** for minerals. With the resonator, for example, budding amethyst grows shards.
The **Cultivator T2** has three lines: put something different in each, and they grow independently. The lines share water, energy, the growth upgrade and the machine upgrades.
Makes what usually drops from mobs, without any mobs. Put in **biomass** and an additive, pour in water and bring heat from the heat network. The additive decides what comes out.
The compressor presses **biomass** out of leaves, seeds, saplings, kelp or sugar cane.
It needs at least 800 heat. If the supply stops, the heat slowly drains and the machine pauses, but it keeps its progress.
They make resources out of power. The **stone generator** produces cobblestone, gravel, sand and obsidian, and the **lava and water generators** fill their tank with fluid.
Turns pure power into **exotic matter**. You put nothing in: feed it power, and every 50M FE one item appears in the output. It takes up to 10M FE per tick, so it needs serious power.
The fabricator itself is made on the magnet, and it takes at least the superconductor coil.
Put a **pusher** in its slot and the matter goes into the neighbouring chest by itself.
